summary: This source is already public definition-spine evidence for Education As A Soul Game and supporting Game Theory method: school is a stakeholder convergence where official learning can become the least rewarded move, and reform only works when it moves inside the actual player game.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: keep this source as the opening definition of school as a stakeholder convergence that turns official learning, literacy, creativity, collaboration, and lifelong learning into status, obedience, parent face, grades, and compliance incentives.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Education owns the formation and soul-output mechanism. Game Theory owns the method of finding players, incentives, power ranking, and overlapping games.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Already public: retain this source as the institutional example in Superstructure Changes The Game, where ideal analysis asks what school should be and game analysis asks what school actually rewards.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Do not duplicate the Education page inside Game Theory. Game Theory needs the source only as method evidence for real rewards, multiple games, and superstructure changing the game.

concept_extensions.proposed_addition: Use only as negative contrast if Living School is revised: Jiang's 2008 program had seminars, books, a coffee house, newspaper, transparency, innovation, and openness, but a successful reform still failed when stakeholders did not accept or control the new game.
concept_extensions.boundary_note: Living School owns the positive school-building dream. This source's active mechanism is why a good school reform can be rejected by the existing school game.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-01-08, before the later trust-test, immigration, compliance, creativity, and living-school updates, Jiang gives the public Education page its core school-game definition: official school purposes are inverted when stakeholder incentives reward status, face, compliance, grades, and minimum work over learning.

The lecture retrospectively dates Jiang's 2008 South China reform as a working predecessor to later school-building pressure, but also marks his later correction: he had built a better game than the stakeholders wanted to play.

This is the second Game Theory class after the January 6 dating-game opening. It adds institutional player analysis, player-power ranking, overlapping games, and superstructure as the source of stakeholder interests.
